title: Application for Vacant Positions
office: CHRMO – Personnel Transaction Division
transaction_type: G2C – Government to Citizen; G2G – Government to Government
who_may_avail: All qualified internal and external applicants

requirements.requirement: Application Letter (indicating the position and item number applied for) addressed to the City Human Resource Management Officer
Personal Data Sheet (CS Form No. 212) with Work Experience Sheet
Academic Credentials (Transcript of Records and Diploma, or any Certification indicating the number of units completed)
Certificate of Eligibility/Ratings/License
requirements.where_to_secure: PRC, CSC, or other government agencies granting eligibility or license to practice profession

requirements.requirement: Performance Ratings in the last two (2) rating periods (if previously employed; not required if previous employer has no existing performance evaluation system or applicant was not employed)

process_flow.client_step: Submit application requirements via email
process_flow.agency_action: Receive application and other requirements and check for completeness.
Evaluate the requirements vis-à-vis the prescribed CGC Competency-based Qualification Standards
Notify the applicant of the results of the evaluation. If qualified, invite to attend assessment activities
process_flow.processing_time: 3 working days after the end of the publication period

process_flow.client_step: If qualified, attend assessment activities.
process_flow.agency_action: Conduct the assessment activities
Consolidate the results of the assessment activities and transmit the results and the appropriate rating sheets to the HRMPSB for rating
Rate all applicants individually based on their assessment results
Consolidate the ratings and prepare comparative assessment results matrix and Selection Line-up
Deliberate on the results of the comparative assessment and finalize the selection line-up for the appropriate action of the appointing authority
Prepare and sign the HRMPSB Resolution and Minutes
Transmit the selection line-up and the signed resolution and minutes to the appointing authority for formal selection.
Select the applicant to be appointed to the vacant position
Notify the applicants of the selection results
process_flow.processing_time: 3 working days upon receipt of selection results

notes: The applicant may be required to attend more than one assessment activity depending on the level of position.

Pursuant to CSC ORA-OHRA, the appointing authority may select among the most qualified candidates within the nine (9) months validity of the publication of the position, otherwise, the position shall be republished.

Confirmed via manual re-check: source document's TOTAL row lists fee as "None" with no total processing time given (the process is asynchronous/depends on HRMPSB scheduling) — this is a genuine source gap, not an extraction error.

process_flow.client_step: 1. Isumite ang nasagutang application form at lahat ng mga kinakailangan dokumento sa BPTFO. Tanggapin ang Statement of Account at magtungo sa bayaran
process_flow.agency_action: 1.1 Tanggapin, suriin at beripikahin ang isinumiteng application form at lahat ng ipinasang mga dokumento at requirements
1.2 Beripikahin ang previous records ng aplikante
1.3 Ipasa ang application form at lahat ng dokumentong kalakip nito sa mga sumusunod na regulatory offices:
1.3.1 CPDO – Pagsusuri ng dokumento at Locational Clearance kung kailangan
1.3.2 BRSO – Pagsusuri ng dokumento at pagbibigay ng bayarin para sa building fees
1.3.3 CENRO – Pagsusuri ng dokumento
process_flow.person_responsible: City Environment & Natural Resources Office (B.O.S.S. Area)

process_flow.agency_action: 1.3.4 CHO – Pagsusuri ng dokumento at kung kailangan, ang mga requirements tulad ng Medical, Mga Resulta sa Laboratory, at iba pa
1.3.5 TOURISM – Pagsusuri ng dokumento
1.3.6 BFP – Pagsusuri ng dokumento
1.3.7 POSO – Pagsusuri ng dokumento at kung kailangan ng safety & traffic clearance
1.3.8 ASSESSOR – Pagsusuri ng dokumento at tax declaration

1.4 Kung compliant ang aplikasyon ito ay i-encode sa system at ipapasa sa treasury. Compliant – kung may valid at kumpletong mga requirements. Not Compliant – kung ang mga requirements ay invalid o may kakulangan; ang mga findings sa application ay isulat sa Document Pre Assessment Form at talakayin sa aplikante
1.5 CTO – I-bill para makabuo ng Statement of Account

process_flow.client_step: 2. Magtungo sa counter ng City Treasury na matatagpuan sa B.O.S.S Area at bayaran ang mga kaukulang bayarin
process_flow.agency_action: 2. Tanggapin ang bayad at bigyan ng kopya ng opisyal na resibo at cedula kung applicable sa kliyente
process_flow.fee: Ayon sa isinasaad ng Calamba City Tax Code of 2006 na nakadisplay sa bulletin board at Facebook Page ng BPTFO

process_flow.client_step: 3. Tanggapin mula sa releasing personnel ang kopya ng Business Permit, Barangay Clearance, Sanitary Permit, Business Plate, stickers at iba pang mga dokumento
process_flow.agency_action: 3.1 CHO – Magprint ng Sanitary Permit
3.2 Mag-print at ibigay sa kliyente ang orihinal na kopya ng Business Permit, Barangay Business Clearance, Plate, Sanitary Permit, Stickers at iba pang mga dokumento

total_fee: Ayon sa isinasaad ng Calamba City Tax Code of 2006
notes: Bago makapag-umpisa ng negosyo ay kinakailangan muna itong iparehistro sa City Government ng Calamba, sa pamamagitan ng pagkuha ng Mayor's / Business Permit. Ang pagkakaroon ng business permit ay magsisiguro na ang operasyon ng negosyo ay sumusunod sa batas at patakaran ng lungsod. Ang BPTFO at iba pang regulatory offices ay mag-eevaluate ng isinumiteng aplikasyon at requirements at maaaring magsagawa ng actual verification ng mga impormasyong inilagay sa application form. Ang mga verifier ay magbibigay ng remarks sa computer system o mga instructions sa susunod na hakbang, ayon sa resulta ng kanilang inspection. Para sa onsite processing by schedule, maaaring pumunta sa online.calambacity.gov.ph para makapag-set ng appointment. Mayroon pang ibang Pre-Requirements para sa ibang uri ng COMPLEX NA NEGOSYO na makikita sa dulong bahagi ng Citizen's Charter. title: City Profile: Overview, Contact Information, and Geography
text: Calamba, officially the City of Calamba, is a 1st class component city in the province of Laguna, Philippines, and serves as the regional center of the CALABARZON region. According to the 2020 census, it has a population of 539,671. Contact: New City Hall Complex, Bacnotan Road, Brgy. Real, City of Calamba, Laguna, 4027; (049) 545-6789; info@calambacity.gov.ph. Geographically, Calamba is bounded by Laguna de Bay to the east, Cabuyao to the north, Los Baños to the south, and Sto. Tomas and Tanauan (Batangas) to the west. It is only 54 kilometers from Metro Manila and is considered the premier industrial hub outside Metro Manila due to the large number of companies based there. Total land area is 14,480 hectares, with an urban expansion area of 8,526.7 hectares, covering 54 barangays (37 urban, 17 rural). As of the 2010 NSO count, total population was 389,377 with 223,241 registered voters. Major religious denominations: Roman Catholic (89.72%), Protestant (3.43%), Iglesia Ni Cristo (3.14%), Islam (0.26%), Others (3.45%). Land use breakdown (in hectares): Urban Redevelopment Area 2,080; Growth Management Area 1: 4,199; Growth Management Area 2: 2,460; Upland Conservation Area: 3,401.22; Forest Buffer Zone: 333; Forest Reservation Area: 579.78; Agricultural Development Area: 1,427; total 14,480 has. Basic facilities include 6 hospitals, 111 clinics, 9 diagnostic centers, 2 public markets, 3 recreational facilities, and 23 transportation facilities. Power supply is provided by Meralco and Napocor; water by Calamba Water District. Telecom providers include Globe, Smart, and SunCellular (cellular) and PLDT, Digitel, SunCellular (landline), with postal service via the Philippine Postal Corporation. Educational institutions include 16 technical/vocational schools, 17 universities and colleges, 21 public and 39 private high schools, and 51 public and 69 private elementary schools.

title: Historical Background and Legal Basis of Creation
text: Calamba was originally part of Tabuco (now Cabuyao) and became a separate pueblo on August 28, 1742 by Governatorial Decree. According to legend, the name 'Calamba' derives from 'kalan-banga,' referring to an earthen jar (banga) a young woman was carrying when a Guardia Civil asked for the name of the place; her answer about what she carried was mistaken for the place name, and 'Kalambanga' was later shortened to 'Calamba.' Calamba became a component city on April 21, 2001 by virtue of Republic Act No. 9024, signed into law by President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo on March 5, 2001 and ratified by plebiscite on April 21, 2001.

title: Economic Data
text: Calamba is classified as a First Class Component City. Annual income by year: 2015 – Php 2.59 Billion; 2014 – Php 2.2 Billion; 2013 – Php 1.95 Billion; 2012 – Php 1.7 Billion. Major income sources include manufacturing (industrial companies), agriculture (rice, corn, vegetables, root crops), services (manpower, metal craft), and tourism (hot spring resorts, Wonder Island, Rizal Shrine).

title: Tourist Destinations, Special Events, and Sister Cities
text: Notable tourist destinations include the Tallest Rizal Monument, hot springs, Wonder Island, Rizal Shrine, industrial parks, and clay pot (Banga) craftmaking. Special events and festivals include: April 21 – City Hood Anniversary/Banga Festival; June 12–19 – Buhayani Festival; June 12 – Independence Day; June 19 – Rizal Day/Rizal's Birth Anniversary; June 24 – Feast of St. John the Baptist/Basaan Festival; August 28 – Town Foundation of Calamba; December (month-long) – Paskuhan sa Calamba; December 30 – Rizal's Death Anniversary. Calamba's sister cities are Walnut City, California, USA; Wilhelmsfeld, Germany; Guri, South Korea; Geumcheon-gu, South Korea; and Litomerice, Czech Republic.

title: Political Data
text: The seat of government is the New City Hall Building, Brgy. Real, City of Calamba. Calamba is the lone congressional district of Laguna. As of August 2013, there were 723 clustered voting precincts.

title: History of Calamba's Cityhood (Republic Act No. 9024)
text: April 21, 2001 marked Calamba's conversion into the second component city of Laguna under Republic Act No. 9024, 'An Act Converting the Municipality of Calamba, Province of Laguna into a Component City to be known as the City of Calamba,' signed by President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo on March 5, 2001 at Malacañang Palace. COMELEC set the ratifying plebiscite for April 21, 2001, three weeks ahead of local elections. The push for cityhood began as early as 1994 when the Sangguniang Bayan passed Resolution No. 60 requesting Congress to co-sponsor a cityhood bill; Resolution No. 115 followed two years later. House Bill No. 986 and Senate Bill Nos. 1630 and 1791 were later filed by Congressman Joaquin M. Chipeco Jr. and Senators Franklin M. Drilon and Sergio Osmeña III respectively. The effort was fast-tracked in 2000 under then-Mayor Severino J. Lajara, with committee approval, public hearings (including one at Calamba Elementary School Central II), and eventual passage as House Bill No. 10661 and, in February 2001, as Republic Act No. 9024. The cityhood campaign involved posters, streamers, barangay patrol announcements, SPES student volunteers distributing flyers, bilingual brochures and comic strips from the City/Municipal Planning and Development Office, and information campaigns conducted across all 54 barangays from March 30 to April 19, 2001, addressing resident questions mainly about taxation and basic services. In the plebiscite, 15,056 Calambeños voted, with 3,413 (22.67%) voting 'No' and the remaining 77.33% voting 'Yes' to cityhood.

text: Calamba City has 54 barangays: Bagong Kalsada, Uno, Dos, Tres, Quatro, Singko, Sais, Syete, Bañadero, Banlic, Barandal, Batino, Bubuyan, Bucal, Bunggo, Burol, Camaligan, Canlubang, Halang, Hornalan, Kay-Anlog, La Mesa, Laguerta, Lawa, Lecheria, Lingga, Looc, Mabato, Majada Labas, Makiling, Mapagong, Masili, Maunong, Mayapa, Milagrosa, Paciano Rizal, Palingon, Palo Alto, Pansol, Parian, Prinza, Punta, Puting Lupa, Real, Saimsim, Sampiruhan, San Cristobal, San Jose, San Juan, Sirang Lupa, Sucol, Turbina, Ulango, and Uwisan.

title: City Government Department List and Functions
text: The City Government of Calamba is organized into the following departments/offices: (1) City Administration Office – supervises city programs and provides administrative support to the Mayor; (2) Business Permits and Tricycle Franchising Office – processes business permits, working permits, and tricycle franchises; (3) City Accounting and Internal Control Office – handles accounting and internal audit; (4) Buildings Regulatory Services Department – enforces the National Building Code (P.D. 1096); (5) City Agricultural Services Department – implements agriculture/aquaculture programs and farmer assistance; (6) City Assessment Office – handles property assessment for local revenue; (7) City Budget Management Office – provides budgetary services; (8) City Civil Registry Office – manages civil registration; (9) City Engineering and Infrastructure Development Department – implements infrastructure projects; (10) City Environment and Natural Resources Office – manages natural resource conservation programs; (11) City General Services Office – provides support services and public facilities; (12) City Health Services Department – implements health programs; (13) City Human Resource and Management Office – manages personnel policy and workforce development; (14) City Planning and Development Office – formulates development plans and policies; (15) City Legal Services Office – provides legal advice and support; (16) City Treasury Management Office – manages city funds and tax collection; (26) City College of Calamba – no valid functional description was provided in the source document for this department (listed description was a duplicate of the Buildings Regulatory Services Department entry).

title: Mission and Vision
text: Commitment and Direction: Shaping a smart, green, and inclusive future for every Calambeño. Mission: Work in partnership with its citizenry to deliver exceptional, effective, fiscally responsible, and gender-responsive services while preserving and protecting the environment and enhancing a high standard of community living. Vision: Calamba is a smart and green city with a progressive and inclusive economy where healthy, empowered, and God-centered people live in a secure, built, and natural environment under good governance.

title: Handling of Cases of Child Victims of Various Forms of Abuse
title_filipino: Paghawak ng kaso ng mga bata na biktima ng iba't-ibang uri ng pang-aabuso
office: City Social Services Department - Special Social Services Division
who_may_avail: Children who are victims of various forms of abuse, exploitation, or trafficking covered by RA 7610 and similar laws

requirements.requirement: Blotter Report
Personal Statement
Birth Certificate
Medico-legal / genital examination result

process_flow.client_step: Go to the City Social Services Department and report the concern
Submit the Intake Sheet from the Barangay or PNP
process_flow.agency_action: Accept and review the document, and log in the logbook.
Conduct the initial Intake Interview using the WCPU Intake Sheet.

Conduct a risk and safety assessment to determine the appropriate intervention needed. Possible interventions: refer to PNP for a medico-legal/genital examination (if sexual/physical abuse) or a Psychologist (if psychological abuse); accompany to PNP to file a case, with assistance continuing until the court issues its Resolution.

process_flow.client_step: Go to the City Social Services Department for Protective Custody or Reintegration
process_flow.agency_action: Process the required documents. Residential Care Facility: if assessment finds it beneficial for the child to be placed in a residential care facility. Reintegration: if the child can safely be returned to the custody of parents/relatives.
Prepare a community-based treatment plan.

process_flow.client_step: Attend Case Conference with family/relatives
process_flow.agency_action: Conduct the Case Conference.
Conduct the community-based treatment plan.
Monitor and evaluate the treatment plan.
Conduct a Case Conference.
Prepare the Terminal Report.

total_processing_time: No fixed duration, as this depends on the processes carried out by other agencies or institutions involved, the type of case and intervention, and the cooperation of the victim and family with the treatment plan.

title: Mediation Dialogue / Family Conference Assistance
title_filipino: Paghingi ng tulong para sa pag-uusap kaugnay ng suliranin sa pinansyal na suporta o kustodiya ng mga bata (Mediation Dialogue) o pag-uusap kaugnay ng hindi pagkakasundo sa loob ng isang pamilya (Family Conference)
office: City Social Services Department - Special Social Services Division
who_may_avail: Couples (married or not) who have decided to separate and are seeking financial support from a former partner, or couples with disagreements over child custody, or any family member seeking to reach an agreement to resolve a family problem

requirements.requirement: Letter of Invitation
Copy of any Mediation conducted at the barangay
Copy of the Barangay Agreement
Blotter Report
Birth Certificate of children (if available)
Marriage Certificate (if married)

process_flow.client_step: Go to the City Social Services Department and report the concern
process_flow.agency_action: Conduct the initial Intake interview using the WCPU intake Sheet.
Assess the concern.

process_flow.client_step: Give preferred schedule for the dialogue
process_flow.agency_action: Prepare and issue the Letter of Invitation.

process_flow.client_step: Send the Letter of Invitation to the other party
Go to the City Social Services Department on the scheduled date for the dialogue
process_flow.agency_action: Conduct the dialogue between both parties.

process_flow.client_step: Sign the agreement
process_flow.agency_action: Prepare the agreement, re-explain the outcome of the dialogue, and have both parties sign.
Monitor and evaluate compliance of both parties with the agreement.
Call both parties after a month and conduct a home visit after three months.
Prepare the Progress Report.

process_flow.client_step: If no agreement was reached and one party wishes to file a case: wait for the referral letter from the Social Worker
process_flow.agency_action: Prepare and issue the Referral Letter to be brought to the Public Attorney's Office.

process_flow.client_step: Receive the Referral Letter and bring it to the Public Attorney's Office

total_processing_time: No fixed duration, as this depends on when the client delivers the Letter of Invitation to the other party, and the cooperation of both parties regarding the agreement reached.

title: Handling Cases of Women and their Children who are Victims of Abuse under RA 9262
title_filipino: Pag-aasikaso ng kaso ng mga babae at kanilang anak na biktima ng pang-aabuso na saklaw ng RA 9262
office: City Social Services Department - Special Social Services Division
who_may_avail: Women and their children who are victims of abuse or violence covered by RA 9262

requirements.requirement: Birth Certificate
Marriage Certificate (if married)
Phone call or letter from partner agencies or other Social Welfare Agencies
Valid ID
Medico-Legal / Genital Examination Result
Blotter Report

process_flow.client_step: Go to the City Social Services Department and report the concern
Submit the Intake Sheet from the barangay or PNP
process_flow.agency_action: Accept and review the document.
Conduct the initial intake interview using the WCPU intake sheet and risk and safety assessment.

process_flow.client_step: Go to the PNP for Medico-Legal/Genital Examination, or to a Psychologist for Psychological Assessment
process_flow.agency_action: Accompany client to PNP for the examination. If needed, refer to a Psychologist for Psychological Assessment.

process_flow.client_step: Go to the PNP and Office of the Clerk of Court with the Social Worker
process_flow.agency_action: Provide the appropriate intervention based on the victim's needs: if not filing a case, assist in obtaining a Protection Order for the victim; if filing a case, accompany to PNP for a sworn statement and to the Office of the Clerk of Court to file the case; if protective custody is needed, process the required documents for a residential care facility; if returning to family, conduct Reintegration and coordinate with the C/MSWDO of their area, requesting a PCAR for possible reunification, and refer to financial assistance if the family cannot cover travel expenses.
process_flow.processing_time: No fixed duration; 1 day for reintegration coordination steps

process_flow.agency_action: Provide additional assistance if needed.
Obtain feedback from other Social Welfare Agencies if the victim was referred to another LGU.

total_processing_time: No fixed duration, as this depends on the processes carried out by other agencies or institutions involved, the type of case and intervention, and the cooperation of the victim and family with the treatment plan.

title: Handling of Foundling, Abandoned, and Voluntarily/Involuntarily Committed Children
title_filipino: Pag-aasikaso sa batang napulot (foundling), pinabayaan (abandoned), boluntaryo / hindi boluntaryong ipinaubayang bata (voluntary / involuntary committed)
office: City Social Services Department - Special Social Services Division
who_may_avail: Foundling, abandoned, or voluntarily/involuntarily committed children

requirements.requirement: Blotter Report
Deed of Voluntary Commitment
Personal Statement of the person who found the child
Foundling Certificate
Medical Report
Birth Certificate

process_flow.client_step: Go to the City Social Services Office and report the concern
Submit the Intake Sheet from the barangay or PNP
process_flow.agency_action: Accept and review the document, and log in the logbook.
Conduct the initial Intake Interview using the WCPU Intake Sheet.
Report to the Barangay or PNP for the Blotter Report.

Process the requirements needed to temporarily place the child in a residential care facility. If the child is voluntarily committed/surrendered/neglected/abandoned, first request a Deed of Voluntary Commitment (DVC).
Process the documents needed to immediately transfer the child to a Child-Caring/Child-Placing Agency (CCA/CPA).
Continue coordination with the CCA/CPA to complete all required documents.

total_processing_time: No fixed duration, as this depends on the availability of a Child Caring/Placing Agency to which the child can be transferred and the time needed to process the various requirements requested by the CCA/CPA.

title: Psychosocial Support Assistance
title_filipino: Paghingi ng tulong para sa Psychosocial Support
office: City Social Services Department - Special Social Services Division
who_may_avail: Children or women in need of psychosocial support within the office's clientele category

requirements.requirement: Intake Sheet Form
Medical History
Birth Certificate
Blotter Report
PWD ID (if any)
requirements.where_to_secure: Persons with Disability Affairs Office (City Hall)

process_flow.client_step: Go to the City Social Services Office to request psychosocial intervention or counseling
process_flow.agency_action: Conduct the initial Intake Interview.

Conduct the initial Assessment. If needed: refer to a Clinical Psychologist or Psychometrician for Psychological Testing. If not needed: assess the client's situation to determine the appropriate intervention.

Conduct the recommended intervention based on the initial Assessment Report. (If serious behavioral manifestation is observed mid-session, the client is advised to seek additional medical intervention from another institution.)
process_flow.processing_time: 1 hour per session, per agreed schedule

process_flow.agency_action: Issue a Certificate of Completion and prepare a Terminal Report once the child's behavioral condition has stabilized and counseling sessions are concluded.

total_processing_time: No fixed duration, as this depends on the processes carried out by other agencies or institutions involved, the type of case and intervention, and the cooperation of the victim and family with the treatment plan.

title: Assistance for Children-at-Risk (CAR) and Children in Conflict with the Law (CICL)
title_filipino: Pagtulong sa Pag-aasikaso sa mga batang nanganganib na magkaroon ng suliranin sa batas (Child-at-Risk) at batang may suliranin sa batas (Children in Conflict with the Law o CCL)
office: City Social Services Department - Special Social Services Division
transaction_type: G2G - Government to Government; G2C - Government to Citizen
who_may_avail: PNP, Barangay, or other agencies with custody of a CICL, or the parent/guardian of the child

requirements.requirement: Birth Certificate
Barangay Blotter
Sworn Statement from PNP
Case Information from the City Prosecutor's Office
Assessment on Discernment (Note: for Child-at-Risk cases, only a Barangay Blotter is needed)

process_flow.client_step: Go to the City Social Services Department and report the concern (Barangay/BWCPD)
process_flow.agency_action: Accept and review the documents.
Conduct the initial Intake Interview and explain the outcome of the CICL's violation of the law.
Conduct the risk and safety assessment to determine whether the child should be referred to a residential care facility or returned to family custody.
Assess the situation and determine appropriate interventions for the child.
Conduct proceedings related to the community-based or center-based treatment plan and prepare a copy of the contract.

process_flow.client_step: Sign the Contract
process_flow.agency_action: Explain the contents of the contract and have participants sign it.

process_flow.client_step: Actively participate in the Interventions
process_flow.agency_action: Conduct the Intervention Program.
process_flow.processing_time: 6 months to 1 year or more, depending on assessment

process_flow.agency_action: Monitor the Intervention Program through case review, case conference, and home visitation.
Prepare the Progress Report.
Prepare a Letter of Request for PCAR if the program's objective has been achieved, and submit it to the Person-in-Charge or other Social Welfare Agency.
process_flow.processing_time: Within one month before the scheduled conference date

process_flow.agency_action: Follow up on the result of the PCAR.

process_flow.client_step: Attend the Case Conference
process_flow.agency_action: Conduct the Case Conference to assess the child's progress.
Conduct the Exit Conference and prepare related documentation.
Prepare the Termination Report.

total_processing_time: No fixed duration, as this depends on the processes carried out by other agencies or institutions involved, the type of case and intervention, and the cooperation of the victim and family with the treatment plan.

title: Conducting an Emergency Reach-Out Operation
title_filipino: Pagsasagawa ng Agarang Reach-Out Operation
office: City Social Services Department - Special Social Services Division
who_may_avail: Children or women who are victims of abuse or violence covered by RA 7610, RA 9262, and similar laws

requirements.requirement: Phone call or letter from partner agencies or other Social Welfare Agencies
Blotter Report
Marriage Certificate
Birth Certificate
Valid ID

process_flow.client_step: Call or go to the City Social Services Office to request an Emergency Rescue
process_flow.agency_action: Answer the call or receive the request.
Accept and review the documents.

Conduct the Risk and Safety Assessment. If the child's/victim's life is not in danger per the assessment: provide the appropriate intervention based on need. If the assessment finds a reach-out operation is needed: conduct the reach-out operation.
Conduct the initial Intake Interview with the rescued child/victim.

If the child/victim requires a Medico-Legal/Physical Examination: refer to PNP. If not required: process the documents needed to bring the child/victim to a residential care facility and provide protective custody, including preparing an After Reach-Out Operation Report and Social Case Study Report.
Accompany the victim to the PNP for the process of filing a case.

total_processing_time: No fixed duration, as this depends on the type and severity of the victim's situation or case and the distance to their location.

title: Foster Care Application
title_filipino: Pag-aasikaso ng Foster Care Application
office: City Social Services Department - Special Social Services Division
who_may_avail: Petitioners who wish to become a Foster Care Parent/Family

requirements.requirement: Certificate of Attendance/Participation
Certificate of Live Birth
Marriage Certificate, or Divorce/Declaration of Nullity of Marriage/Legal Separation documents
Medical Certificate issued within 6 months from time of application
Latest Income Tax Return or Certificate of Employment or other proof of income
Original copy of NBI/Police Clearance issued within a year from date of application
Original copy of Barangay Certificate stating residency, length of residence, and good moral character
Whole Body Picture taken within 6 months of application, with date indicated
Photograph of interior and exterior of the applicant's house
Philhealth ID (photocopy) and updated Members Data Record or HMO record (if HMO allows declaring a foster child as dependent)
Written consent of biological children aged 10 and above living in the household
Signed Undertaking on Child Protection Code and Code of Conduct of Foster Parents
Certificate of Attendance at Foster Care Forum (digital copy accepted)
Original copy of letters from 3 non-relative Character References who have known the applicant for at least 3 years
Such other documents that the NACC, CPA, or LGU may require

process_flow.client_step: Attend the Online Forum (client/petitioner)
process_flow.agency_action: Provide the RACCO Online Forum link.

process_flow.client_step: Fill out the Undertaking and Application Form
Have the required documents reviewed before submitting to RACCO
process_flow.agency_action: Review the documents and assist the client/petitioner in completing them.
Conduct home visitation and interview once the letter from RACCO is received, to gather information needed for the Home Study Report.
Prepare the Foster Care Home Study Report and submit to RACCO.
Go to the RACCO Office and submit the Foster Care Application.
Wait for RACCO's decision and request copies of submitted documents plus the recommendation letter.

process_flow.client_step: Wait for the application result (may file a Motion for Reconsideration)
process_flow.agency_action: If approved: RACCO issues the Foster Care License and Identification Card. If not approved: assist the petitioner in completing requirements per RACCO's recommendation.

total_processing_time: No fixed duration, as this depends on how quickly the client can complete the required documents and on the processes carried out at the Regional Alternative Child Care Office (RACCO).

title: Application for Adoption (Regular Case)
title_filipino: Aplikasyon para sa Adoption (Regular na kaso)
office: City Social Services Department - Special Social Services Division
who_may_avail: Petitioners at least 25 years old who have the legal capacity to assume parental rights over a child

requirements.requirement: Certificate of Attendance/Participation
Application and Undertaking Form
Authenticated or SECPA copy of applicant's birth record

Authenticated or SECPA copy of Marriage Certificate and/or CENOMAR, or (if marriage terminated) authenticated divorce papers with court decision, Certificate of Finality, Declaration of Nullity, or Legal Separation documents
Written consent from the appropriate person(s)

Medical evaluation form with test results and Medical Certification (taken at least 6 months before preparation of the Home Study Report) confirming no medical condition preventing parental responsibilities
Psychological evaluation report on the applicant(s), as recommended by the social worker
NBI or Police Clearance or Court Clearance issued within one year before filing
Latest Income Tax Return or document showing financial capacity
Letters attesting to character and general reputation from at least 3 non-related character references (one preferably an employer or business associate)
5R-sized photos of applicant(s), immediate family, and their home, taken within the last 6 months and dated
Certificate of Finality (if with a previously adopted child)

process_flow.client_step: Attend the Pre-Adoption Online Forum
process_flow.agency_action: Provide the Pre-Adoption Online Forum link from RACCO.

process_flow.client_step: Complete all required documents and submit to RACCO
process_flow.agency_action: Assist the Petitioner in completing the required documents.

process_flow.client_step: Wait for the letter from RACCO indicating the Home Study Report may begin
process_flow.agency_action: Conduct home visitation, interview, and counseling, and prepare the Home Study Report.
Submit the Home Study Report to RACCO.

process_flow.client_step: Wait for the Letter/Memorandum containing comments on the application and submitted documents
Follow RACCO's recommendations or comments
process_flow.agency_action: Assist the petitioner in completing documents requested by RACCO.

process_flow.client_step: Go to RACCO's Office and submit the application
process_flow.agency_action: Accompany the petitioner to RACCO's Office.

process_flow.client_step: Wait for the letter with the decision on the application; request copies of submitted documents with the letter from RACCO

total_processing_time: No fixed duration, as this depends on how quickly the client can complete the required documents and on the processes carried out at the Regional Alternative Child Care Office (RACCO).

title: Application for Step-Parent, Relative, and Adult Adoption
title_filipino: Aplikasyon para sa Step-Parent, Relative and Adult Adoption
office: City Social Services Department - Special Social Services Division
who_may_avail: Petitioners at least 25 years old who have the legal capacity to assume parental rights over a child

requirements.requirement: Certificate of Attendance/Participation
Child Case Study Report and Home Case Study Report or Social Case Study Report, whichever applies
Copies of birth record of the PAP(s) and the child
Copies of Marriage Certificate and/or CENOMAR, or (if terminated) authenticated divorce/annulment/nullity/legal separation documents
NBI or Police Clearance or Court Clearance; if foreign national, clearance from police where lived more than 12 months in the past 15 years
Copy of the Death Certificate of the child's biological parents, if applicable
Written consent of the child aged 10 or over
Written consent of marital/adopted children of the PAP(s) aged 10 or over
Written consent of non-marital children aged 10 or over living with or under the parental authority of the PAP(s)
Written consent of the biological parent or person exercising substitute parental authority over the child to be adopted (not required if adoptee is already an adult)
Result of recent medical evaluation of the child and PAP(s) prepared within 6 months prior to application (may be waived if adoptee is an adult)
Psychological evaluation of the PAP(s) prepared within 2 years
Psychological evaluation of the child (for children 5 and above) prepared within 2 years, as recommended by the social worker
Letter attesting to character and reputation from at least 3 non-related character references
Recent 5R close-up and whole-body pictures of the adoptee and PAP(s) taken within the last 6 months, dated
Documents showing the financial capacity of the PAP(s)

process_flow.client_step: Attend the Online Pre-Adoption Forum
process_flow.agency_action: Provide the Pre-Adoption Forum link from RACCO.

If Relative Adoption: attempt to locate biological parents via Tri-Media posting or letter, seeking consent for the adoption. Once located, conduct a Parenting Capability Assessment. Prepare the Social Case Study Report.

total_processing_time: No fixed duration, as this depends on how quickly the client can complete the required documents and on the processes carried out at the Regional Alternative Child Care Office (RACCO).
